goal_text: (Reused from research_synth_027) Compare five mechanistic theories of biological aging — telomere shortening, mitochondrial dysfunction, cellular senescence, proteostasis failure, and epigenetic drift — on supporting evidence and one key limitation of each.
ground_truth: 1. Telomere shortening (Hayflick, Blackburn): replicative senescence triggered by telomere erosion in dividing cells; evidence: telomerase extends replicative lifespan; limitation: many aging effects occur in post-mitotic cells. 2. Mitochondrial dysfunction (Harman free radical theory): ROS damage mtDNA and proteins; evidence: mtDNA mutations accumulate with age; limitation: antioxidant supplementation does not extend lifespan in most studies. 3. Cellular senescence (Campisi): SASP promotes chronic tissue inflammation; evidence: clearing senescent cells in mice improves healthspan; limitation: some senescent cells are beneficial in wound healing and embryogenesis. 4. Proteostasis failure (Balch et al.): chaperone and autophagy capacity declines, causing toxic protein aggregates; evidence: linked to Alzheimer's and Parkinson's pathology; limitation: difficult to separate cause from effect in neurodegeneration. 5. Epigenetic drift (Horvath clock): DNA methylation patterns diverge from youthful state; evidence: Horvath methylation clock predicts biological age with <5 year error; limitation: methylation changes may be a biomarker rather than a causal driver.
